intro.name: Two plans
intro.text:
Two skilled gardeners have developed different plans for a small community garden near the village. (Gardener1) favors {A.1}, while (gardener2) favors {A.2}.
An elder says that both plans have merit. A child asks whether there will be room to play. A nursing mother nearby suggests a place where parents can sit with their babies while older children explore safely.

choices.label: Combine the best features into one shared garden.
Give each gardener a small plot to demonstrate the plan.

s1.text: The gardeners cooperate, creating a beautiful and useful space.

s2.text: They argue over the path's exact shape, then compromise when the elder suggests a curved path with straight planting beds.

s3.text: A child draws an elaborate map featuring a "secret frog kingdom." The gardeners reserve a small corner for wildlife.

s4.text: The gardeners realize that the combined plan needs more work than they can manage. They simplify it rather than overpromise.

p1.text: Both gardens flourish in different ways. The villagers learn which designs suit which purposes.

p2.text: One garden produces more food, while the other becomes a favorite resting place. Neither is declared a failure.

p3.text: The gardeners become playful rivals and begin leaving compliments disguised as criticisms.

p4.text: A plant grows across the dividing line. The gardeners spend an absurd amount of time deciding who owns it.
